subject: Post-call: LarkEdge discovery + tech qualification (latency / topology asks)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@larkedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + quick asks (LarkEdge)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a short list of asks so we can scope a targeted deep-dive next week.

What we heard (top pain points)
- 95th percentile latency spikes on current LLM inference (customer-facing chat) causing poor UX during peak windows.
- Cost variability: large token bursts when agents require extended contexts and retrievals.
- Need for predictable capacity during promotions (traffic 3x baseline for 10–20min windows).

Goals you stated
- Maintain 95th latency under ~250ms for standard chatbot queries (typical response size ~120 tokens); tolerate higher for long-form generations.
- Sustain 1.5–2k tokens/sec steady-state for the primary region (US-west), with ability to burst to ~6k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Data residency and VPC isolation (SOC 2 required).

Immediate asks to prepare deep technical session
1) Share a 72-hour sample of production request traces (timestamps, request size, model id, upstream latencies) — CSV is fine.
2) Confirm the model family(s) you plan to serve (open LlamaX- or transformer-based proprietary?).
3) Expected concurrent sessions / peak concurrency and typical prompt sizes (tokens).
4) Any hard constraints: on-prem only, strict egress limits, or allowed managed VPC?

Attachments: larkedge-procurement-questions.pdf (your procurement list) — I referenced a few items during the call.

Proposed next step: Marissa (our Solutions Engineer) and I can run a topology sketch & cost/latency projection once we have the traces + model info. Would Wed 07 May 09:00 PT work for a 60–75 minute hands-on topology workshop with your SREs?

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick asks (LarkEdge)

Jordan — solid recap, thanks. Confirming and adding a couple notes from our side.

Confirmations
- Model family: primary is LarkEdge-XL (proprietary, distillation of open transformer) for customer-facing chat; internal reranking uses open Llama variants.
- Target: 95th latency ~250ms for common queries (~<150 tokens); tiered SLA for long-form.
- Security: SOC 2 plus customer-managed KMS (preferred). VPC peering or Private deployment is acceptable; looking for KMS/HSM integration.

We will share the 72-hour traces (anonymized) — attaching traffic export. Expect to include concurrent session counts and a short legend for event columns.

Timeline: engineering wants a clear recommendation by mid-June so procurement can start procurement/contract work; ideal prod target is Q3.

Also: we have internal logs that show KV-cache warm-start is a major variance during long sessions (cache misses spike during campaign bursts). Would like Redwood to comment on cache warmup strategies.

Attachment: larkedge-traffic-patterns.csv

Sam

Subject: Internal: LarkEdge follow-up — topology + SLO proposal notes

Internal notes for the workshop and what we should prepare. Copying into the thread when we have the deck.

Recommended immediate approach (high level)
- Topology: Dedicated pool in US-west for primary LarkEdge-XL traffic with autoscale rules keyed to 95th latency and token/sec thresholds + a cross-region fallback to hosted smaller model variant for spike protection. Consider Private (VPC) deployment if KMS/HSM integration is mandatory.
- Autoscale knobs: target sustained throughput 2k tokens/sec, burst policy to 6k tokens/sec for windows up to 15 mins with queue-length mitigation.
- Latency SLOs: aim for p95 generation <250ms for standard prompts (<=150 tokens). p99 should be flagged as best-effort with throttling policies.
- Caching: propose prefix and KV-cache pre-warming strategy tied to campaign identifiers; instrumentation to measure cache-hit delta during promotions.

Technical artifacts to bring to the deep-dive
1) Topology sketch (edge routing, dedicated shard placement, fallback paths) — see attached redwood-topology-sketch.png.
2) Simulated load plan for the 72-hour sample (batch sizes, concurrency sweep, warm vs cold cache).
3) Test harness access: we’ll request a short window to run synthetic loads (non-prod) against a canary config.

Calendar: Jordan proposed Wed 07 May 09:00 PT — I can run the session and bring the SRE lead. We should also invite Neha for procurement / contract framing (pricing buckets for bursts).

Open questions for Sam to confirm before the session
- Can they share golden prompt examples for quality tuning?
- Are there hard egress bandwidth caps for third-party egress?

Marissa
